title: Stranded passenger
text: {ship} calls in on a thin carrier wave. Their drive is cooked, and one passenger would very much like to be somewhere else. "I'll pay, and I'll be no trouble. Mostly."

outcomes.text: A tired passenger climbs through the lock, thanks you twice and asks if the galley has tea.
You sign off. The carrier wave hangs in the static a little longer than it should.

title: A courier's lost parcel
text: A courier on the {system} lane has lost a sealed parcel and the nerve to explain it to her employer. "It's small, it's dull, and it's late. Could you carry it?"

outcomes.text: The parcel is no heavier than a loaf. You decide not to wonder what is in it.
"Understood," she says, in the voice of someone rehearsing an apology.

title: Pedlar with a bargain
text: {ship} drifts alongside with a hold full of crates and a smile that has seen many sales. "Food, fresh enough, ten tons for 400. You won't get kinder prices this side of a famine."

outcomes.text: "Your loss," the pedlar sighs, "and quite possibly your lunch."

title: Cargo adrift
text: A string of loose crates tumbles slowly through the dark, their tags faded to nothing. Somebody lost a shift's worth of work here.

outcomes.text: Eight tons of machine parts, still sealed. Finders keepers, in the oldest tradition.
You leave the crates to their slow tumble.

title: An empty derelict
text: A dead hull turns on its axis, airlocks open, bunks made. Whoever left did it neatly and in no hurry.

outcomes.text: Nothing but a folded blanket and a pencil stub. You take neither and feel faintly respectful.
A derelict near {system} was left tidy and unlooted. Crews say the lanes there are kinder than they look.

title: A derelict worth stripping
text: A gutted freighter hangs in the dark, her hold doors torn open. Most of her went long ago, but not all.

outcomes.text: A salvage broker pays for the beacon code without asking where it came from.
You nod to the wreck and fly on.

title: Hauler running dry
text: {ship}, a slow hauler, is coasting on fumes. "One lane short of the next pump, friend. I'd be glad of twenty units, and I'll pay, or I'll owe you."

outcomes.text: "I'll tell every dock I pass that you're a decent sort," the hauler's captain promises.
"No hard feelings," says the hauler, in a tone that suggests a few.

title: A surveyor's beacon
text: A small beacon blinks on the empty edge of {system}, still faithfully pinging a chart nobody collects. Its data crystal is a snap to pull.

outcomes.text: The nearest lanes unfold on your map, neatly ruled and slightly out of date.
The beacon keeps blinking at nothing, as it has for years.

title: A rumour on the air
text: {ship} is broadcasting to anybody who'll listen, which today is you. It is the sort of gossip that keeps lanes interesting.

outcomes.text: A trader heard on the {system} lane says prices at the rim ports run high for anyone willing to bring food and medicine.
You mute the broadcast. The silence is restful.

title: Pilgrim convoy
text: A convoy of pilgrims in mismatched hulls files past, singing across all channels. {ship} asks if you can spare a little fuel for the road to the next shrine.

outcomes.text: They bless your ship, tuck a few coins through the line, and resume singing.
The song fades slowly behind you.

title: A customs-free trader
text: {ship} offers four tons of luxury goods at a price that does not mention a tariff, or a receipt. "They fell off a cart," says the trader, "in space. It's a very long fall."

outcomes.text: The trader shrugs and vanishes down a lane that is not on any chart you own.

title: A seller of old charts
text: {ship} sells charts by the dozen, folded as paper in a hold that smells of lamp oil. "Only 300, and you'll know where the quiet lanes go."

outcomes.text: "Suit yourself," says the seller, folding a map into a bird.

title: A surveyor's old call
text: A weak automated hail drifts out of the empty rim: a survey ship's recall code, looping for years, answering nobody. Its heading points where the charts go blank.

outcomes.text: A looping survey recall points from Skerry to a lane the charts never drew. A place called Hushwater lies at the end of it.
The signal repeats once more, patiently, and falls behind you.

title: The Long Patience
text: She drifts in the still water, a survey ship older than the lane she came by. Her running lights are dark but her cabin is clean, and her log is still switched on.

outcomes.text: You hold the Long Patience's log and transponder. A Free Reach shipyard could rebuild a hull like her, given the right captain.
The log lights up as you plug in, and a quiet voice reads her last entry: "Waiting for a pilot. No hurry."
It takes an afternoon. The plating sells well. The silence afterwards is heavy.
You leave her drifting. She has waited this long.

title: A diver with a pearl
text: A diver from Quiet Shoal hails you from an open boat. "We don't sell to just anybody," she says, "but you came here on purpose. One pearl, 600."

outcomes.text: She dips a hand in the water as you go, which you take as courtesy.
